title: Internationalized focus states and color-blend audit for cost dashboards
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Audit and refine interactive focus states, high-contrast color blends, and localization considerations for the Cost Explorer and Rollouts dashboards. Goal is to ensure keyboard navigation, focus visibility, and semantic color usage remain robust across locales (including RTL languages and locales with non-western numeral systems), and that color-blend/opacity layers meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast when composed over dynamic backgrounds.

Problem: Several recent snapshots of the cost-timeline and rollout-variant inspector have marginal focus outlines when the density toggle is set to compact, and some tokenized metric chips use subtle semi-transparent foregrounds that fail contrast tests against vivid cost heatmap gradients in dark mode. In addition, RTL builds shift some focus order heuristics and the numeric abbreviation components occasionally reflow, causing non-linear keyboard traversal.

Proposed scope:
- Audit all interactive components in Cost Explorer, Rollouts Variant Inspector, and Metric Cards for focus visibility at all density modes and both light/dark themes.
- Define a new semantic focus token set (outline-width, offset, and color strategy) that supports internationalization (no icon-only focus traps) and works for both LTR and RTL.
- Replace problematic semi-transparent text layers with color-blend-safe tokens or introduce a layered contrast guideline (foreground-on-gradient checks).
- Prototype keyboard-only flows (tab, shift+tab, arrow nav where applicable) for RTL locales and for controls that use nested composite widgets (chip groups, segmented toggles).
- Update component docs and create a small acceptance test harness (storybook + axe + manual checklist) to validate across locales.

Acceptance criteria:
1) All interactive elements have a visible focus indicator that meets 3:1 minimum visibility above surrounding UI and 4.5:1 contrast for text inside focused controls where text is essential.
2) No contrast failures in automated contrast scans for cost cards and heatmaps in both themes.
3) Keyboard order preserved and announced correctly by screen readers in both LTR and RTL manual tests.
4) Design tokens and usage examples added to the Console design system docs with code snippets and a short migration checklist for engineers.

Tradeoffs/Notes:
- Stronger focus rings increase visual noise for power users; we'll provide a density-aware token so teams can surface lighter indicators in dense layouts while maintaining a minimum accessible threshold.
- For some legacy metric chips, changing opacity may shift perceived weight; we'll pair token changes with microcopy/spacing adjustments to preserve visual hierarchy.

Artifacts:
- Prototype (Figma): https://redwood.design/figma/console-focus-audit-765432 (internal)
- Acceptance checklist (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/Focus+Contrast+Audit+765432
- Storybook branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/tree/feat/a11y-focus-765432

Implementation notes for eng: Use CSS custom properties for the focus tokens, expose a --rw-focus-visual-level to switch density behavior. For RTL, prefer logical order (start/end) for focus offset and avoid absolute left/right pixel nudges. Where gradient overlays exist, compute contrast of flattened composited color in the build step or add a semi-opaque backdrop behind text when necessary.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Initial audit complete: flagged 18 components across cost dashboards; documented examples and captured failing contrast ratios in Confluence.
2026-03-02 - Design sync: agreed on layered-token approach to allow density variants; PM Priya Singh requested explicit acceptance criteria for customer impact cases.
2026-03-05 - Engineering feedback (Liu, ENG-4512): prefers token names to map to existing runtime flags; requested prototype export and Storybook controls for toggling density/theme.

2026-03-08 - Accessibility review (external consultant): recommended increasing focus outline thickness from 2px to 3px for dark-mode low-luminance areas; flagged chip opacity on heatmap as high priority.
2026-03-10 - Submitted PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1892 (includes token updates and Storybook tests); awaiting ENG review and perf check on repaint churn.
2026-03-10 - UX review notes: add screen reader label patterns for collapsed metric chips and ensure numeric abbreviation retains full value in aria-label (e.g., "$1.2M (1,200,000)").
